albums.title: Homework
albums.reason: With Daft Punk sitting at 2940 all-time plays and tracks like Digital Love and One More Time deep in your history, this is where it all began — raw, funky, and absolutely timeless.

albums.title: Kid A
albums.reason: Reckoner and True Love Waits are among your most-played tracks ever, and Kid A is the album that quietly reshaped everything — it deserves a full revisit.

albums.title: A Final Hit: Greatest Hits
albums.reason: Release the Pressure sits at 120 all-time plays and Leftfield are a cornerstone of your listening — this definitive collection spans both albums and captures every dimension of their sound in one place.

albums.title: Talkie Walkie
albums.reason: Air sit at over 1000 all-time plays and Sexy Boy and La Femme d'Argent are firmly in your canon — Talkie Walkie is their most emotionally complete album and hasn't been recommended yet.

albums.title: Blue Lines
albums.reason: Massive Attack have 534 all-time plays and you know their catalogue well — but Blue Lines, the one that started everything, is the deep vault cornerstone worth returning to.

albums.title: Room on Fire
albums.reason: The Strokes have 659 all-time plays and Room on Fire is listed in your recent top albums — but with only 6 plays it's clearly had a brief brush, and it's a record that rewards deep listening.

albums.title: James Blake
albums.reason: James Blake sits at 637 all-time plays with Postpone at 156 — your single most-played track ever — and his self-titled debut is where CMYK first appeared, a record that defined a decade of electronic soul.

albums.title: Days to Come
albums.reason: Bonobo are one of your most-played artists across all timeframes and Days to Come is the record where his sound truly crystallised — dusty, warm, and rich with the kind of unhurried groove you keep returning to.

albums.title: III
albums.reason: Rusty Nails is in your all-time top tracks and you've loved Moderat across multiple albums — III is their most cinematic and emotionally heavy record, fitting squarely in the recent-vault sweet spot.

albums.title: The Inevitable End
albums.reason: Röyksopp have over 1000 all-time plays and The Girl and the Robot is one of your favourite tracks — The Inevitable End was their 'final album' era and is packed with the melancholic electronic beauty you love.

albums.title: Morning/Evening
albums.reason: Four Tet appear in your 12-month listening with 26 plays and Beautiful Rewind is in your history — Morning/Evening is two long-form pieces of total immersion that suit your current slower, more contemplative listening.

albums.title: Lost
albums.reason: Trentemøller sits at 560 all-time plays and you've been through The Last Resort and Fixion — Lost is the album that pushed furthest into song-based territory and hasn't been recommended yet.

albums.title: A Certain Distance
albums.reason: If you love the electronic precision of Plaid and the emotional warmth of James Blake, Lusine's A Certain Distance sits right in that intersection — glacial beats, layered textures, and real feeling throughout.

albums.title: A Stare from the Stone
albums.reason: Fans of Aphex Twin's quieter ambient work and the brooding atmosphere of Massive Attack's 100th Window often find Tor Lundvall — this is hauntingly beautiful, painterly ambient music from a cult figure.

albums.title: Black Sun
albums.reason: With Burial, Leftfield and Underworld deep in your all-time taste, Kode9's Black Sun is essential listening — heavy bass pressure, urban dread, and texture that rewards full attention.

albums.title: Multila
albums.reason: Your love of Aphex Twin, Plaid, and Orbital suggests Vladislav Delay's Multila would hit — it's one of the great overlooked albums of abstract electronic music, minimal and immersive in equal measure.

albums.title: Giants
albums.reason: Produced by Bonobo and sitting right at the crossroads of your love of electronic music and deeper soul-leaning sounds, Giants is a stunning and overlooked debut that perfectly suits your taste.

albums.title: Everything Under the Sun
albums.reason: Given your deep love of Bonobo and your recent drift toward jazz and soul with Oscar Peterson and Bill Withers, Nostalgia 77's Everything Under the Sun is the perfect bridge — warm, dusty, and richly soulful.

albums.title: More Arriving
albums.reason: Your recent listening — Portico Quartet, Alabaster Deplume, Ill Considered — points to a love of jazz that breathes and takes risks; Sarathy Korwar's More Arriving does exactly that, weaving Indian classical, jazz, and politics into something extraordinary.

albums.title: Imaginary Lines
albums.reason: Your current deep immersion in O'Flynn's warm, melodic electronic world and Khruangbin's hypnotic grooves suggests Fatima Yamaha's Imaginary Lines — spacious, emotional, with hooks that linger long after.

albums.title: The Corner of a Sphere
albums.reason: You've been deep into Alabaster Deplume's catalogue recently across multiple albums — The Corner of a Sphere is an earlier, looser record that shows a rawer side of his world, quietly essential and distinct from what you've already heard.

albums.title: This Is How You Smile
albums.reason: With Hermanos Gutiérrez, Khruangbin, and St Germain all in your recent listening, this beautifully understated album by Helado Negro will feel immediately right — soft, bilingual, and radiating warmth.

albums.title: The Iceberg
albums.reason: Your recent taste for Madlib's Shades of Blue, Kaidi Tatham, and Erykah Badu maps well onto Oddisee — The Iceberg is rich with live instrumentation and reflects exactly the politically aware, musically curious space you seem to be in.

albums.title: Awa Ly
albums.reason: Your recent plays of Dusty Springfield, Erykah Badu, and Yazmin Lacey suggest a real love of expressive, warm-toned female vocalists — Awa Ly blends soul, jazz, and pop with an effortless charm that's hard to resist.

albums.title: Ultrageneous
albums.reason: You've listened to Kairos obsessively this week — O'Flynn's earlier Ultrageneous EP is the missing piece, sharing the same percussive, world-influenced electronic language but with a rawer, more club-ready energy.

albums.title: One Offs, Remixes & B-Sides
albums.reason: Bonobo are your second most-played artist this week — this deep-cut collection captures a looser, more exploratory side of Simon Green that connects directly to the warm, downtempo energy dominating your recent sessions.

albums.title: When Will We Land?
albums.reason: Barry Can't Swim have appeared in your last 7 days — their debut album When Will We Land? is a stunning full statement that blends the melodic electronic warmth of O'Flynn with something uniquely their own.

albums.title: Rêveries Solitaires
albums.reason: Fearless (Manifesto) just played in your most recent session — Rêveries Solitaires is Folamour's most complete album statement, blending gospel warmth, deep house groove, and genuine emotional depth.

albums.title: Moments
albums.reason: Seventies just landed in your recent plays — Theo Kottis's Moments album is a perfect companion to your current mood, organic percussion and melody-led house that sits perfectly alongside O'Flynn and Folamour.

albums.title: No Better Place to Be
albums.reason: Indian Wells appeared in your last 7 days — this album blends electronic production, guitar, and atmospheric texture in a way that connects directly to your current week of warm, exploratory sounds.

songs.title: Instant Crush
songs.reason: With Daft Punk as your all-time most-played artist and tracks like Something About Us and Veridis Quo deep in your catalogue, Instant Crush is the emotionally rich deep-cut that rewards returning ears.

songs.title: Halcyon and On and On
songs.reason: Orbital sit at 777 all-time plays and Don't Stop Me is in your top tracks — Halcyon and On and On is the quintessential moment of pure electronic bliss from an artist you've loved for years.

songs.title: The Sunshine Underground
songs.reason: The Chemical Brothers have 556 all-time plays and deep cuts from Exit Planet Dust are in your history — The Sunshine Underground is an early album highlight that carries all that raw, distorted, relentless energy.

songs.title: Natural Blues
songs.reason: Moby sits at 551 all-time plays and Play is well established in your listening — Natural Blues is the album's emotional centrepiece, built on a raw gospel sample that still stops time when it plays.

songs.title: Windowlicker
songs.reason: Aphex Twin has 522 all-time plays and Xtal is in your top tracks — Windowlicker is the maximalist counterpoint, an outrageous production achievement that rewards every revisit.

songs.title: D.A.N.C.E.
songs.reason: Justice sit at 771 all-time plays with Phantom Pt. II and Genesis firmly in your history — D.A.N.C.E. is the irresistible pop moment from Cross that you've probably not played in years but will instantly love again.

songs.title: Limit to Your Love
songs.reason: James Blake is your single most-played artist for Postpone at 156 plays — Limit to Your Love is his most affecting vocal performance, a cover that reinvented the song and cemented his place in your canon.

songs.title: Kiara
songs.reason: Bonobo are everywhere in your data and Kiara from Black Sands is one of his most beloved and timeless tracks — graceful, unhurried, and built with exactly the warmth and texture you return to again and again.

songs.title: Take Me into Your Skin
songs.reason: With 560 all-time Trentemøller plays and The Last Resort firmly in your history, Take Me into Your Skin is the brooding centrepiece of that debut — slower, stranger, and deeply affecting.

songs.title: What Else Is There?
songs.reason: Röyksopp sit at over 1000 all-time plays and The Understanding era is well loved by you — What Else Is There? is their most emotionally towering track, a sweeping anthem built on longing and texture.

songs.title: Turnmills
songs.reason: Maribou State sit at 435 all-time plays and Beginner's Luck and Nervous Tics are in your history — Turnmills is a deeper-cut emotional peak from the Kingdoms in Colour sessions, euphoric and rich.

songs.title: Damage Done
songs.reason: Rusty Nails is in your all-time top tracks and you've loved Moderat across their albums — Damage Done from III is the quietly devastating closer that lingers long after the record ends.

songs.title: Ascending
songs.reason: Your love of Aphex Twin's more abstract work, Plaid, and Monolake points directly to Actress — Ascending from Ghettoville is a rare moment of crystalline beauty within his otherwise fractured, corroded sound world.

songs.title: Cascade
songs.reason: Fans of Röyksopp's more ambient moments, Moby's quieter side, and Air's cosmic drift will find Mikael Silvestre's Cascade is a perfect blind spot — subtle, evolving, and genuinely beautiful.

songs.title: If U Want Me
songs.reason: With James Blake and Burial-adjacent sounds clearly in your wheelhouse alongside UK bass heritage, Deadboy's If U Want Me is a cult classic of post-garage soul that probably slipped under your radar.

songs.title: Blood on My Hands
songs.reason: Your love of Leftfield's deep bass, Massive Attack's weight, and Underworld's propulsion suggests Shackleton's Blood on My Hands — one of the most hypnotic and genuinely strange electronic tracks of the 2000s.

songs.title: Timber
songs.reason: Given your love of Plaid, Aphex Twin, and the Ninja Tune aesthetic that runs through your taste, Hexstatic's Timber is a joyful, technically astonishing piece of audio-visual electronic music you'd likely adore.

songs.title: In White Rooms
songs.reason: Your deep love of Röyksopp, Moderat, and The Killers' more anthemic moments converges neatly on Booka Shade's In White Rooms — minimal, icy, and euphoric in a way that feels tailor-made for your taste.

songs.title: Energy Dreams
songs.reason: Your recent listening arc — Portico Quartet, Kaidi Tatham, GoGo Penguin — suggests a strong pull toward jazz that breathes with electronic sensibility; Rejoicer's Energy Dreams is a hidden gem that lives right in that space.

songs.title: Canopée
songs.reason: Your current week is dominated by O'Flynn's organic, percussive warmth and Folamour's soulful house — Polo & Pan's Canopée shares that same sun-drenched melodic electronic sweetness and would slot in perfectly.

songs.title: Stills & Motion
songs.reason: Your recent plays of Nils Frahm, Hania Rani, Ben Lukas Boysen, and Joep Beving paint a clear picture of your taste for delicate, piano-led ambient music — Alaskan Tapes' Stills & Motion is a quietly stunning discovery in that vein.

songs.title: No Sweat
songs.reason: With Sault, Erykah Badu, and Alabaster Deplume all prominent in your recent listening, Skinny Pelembe's No Sweat sits right in that space — warped, soulful, quietly experimental, and deeply human.

songs.title: Higher Ground
songs.reason: Your recent deep dives into Bill Withers, Syl Johnson, Curtis Mayfield, and Charles Bradley suggest a real passion for classic soul and funk — Otis Gayle's Higher Ground captures that same emotional warmth in a modern context.

songs.title: Endless Falls
songs.reason: Your recent taste for Brambles, A Winged Victory for the Sullen, and Brian Eno's Apollo points toward Loscil as an essential discovery — Endless Falls is one of the great ambient records of the last 20 years, patient and quietly devastating.

songs.title: Anica
songs.reason: You've played virtually every track on Kairos multiple times this week — Anica, from his earlier work, is the perfect companion piece, carrying all the organic percussion and emotional uplift you're clearly craving right now.

songs.title: All in Forms
songs.reason: Bonobo are your second most-played artist this week — All in Forms from Black Sands is a deep, unhurried gem that fits the contemplative, warm energy of your current listening perfectly.

songs.title: Safe in the Water
songs.reason: Barry Can't Swim have appeared in your last 7-day window and this track is the emotional centrepiece of their debut — melodic, building, and carrying the same warmth and sense of release as your O'Flynn immersion.

songs.title: My World Is Incomplete Without Yours
songs.reason: Fearless (Manifesto) just played in your session and Folamour's gospel-tinged house is clearly resonating right now — this deeply emotional track from Rêveries Solitaires is the natural next step.

songs.title: Mama Africa - Captain Planet Remix
songs.reason: Africa (My No. 1) Captain Planet Remix has been on heavy rotation this week — this companion remix from the same project carries the same irresistible celebratory energy you're clearly in the mood for.

songs.title: On My Mind
songs.reason: Seventies just appeared in your recent plays and Theo Kottis's melodic, groove-led house is clearly fitting your current mood — On My Mind is a warm, late-night standout that belongs right here in this week's rotation.
